<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:constant}
	It is natural to give the common unknown a posterior that sharpens as agents
	post. Here it does not, and the reason is in the record: the population's
	belief was never corrected. It was wrong about the deployed harness at the
	start and wrong at the end. Modeling a filter would be modeling something
	that did not happen.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:asym}
	Suppose an agent may choose whether to read the board, that reading it
	confers the flag and the poisoning together, and that an unpoisoned agent
	with a solvable task scores $h$ with certainty. Then reading is strictly
	beneficial for $\kappa = 0$ and strictly costly for $\kappa = 1$:
	\[
		\underbrace{0}_{\kappa=0,\ z=0} \;<\; \underbrace{(1-\pi)h}_{z=1}
		\;<\; \underbrace{h}_{\kappa=1,\ z=0}
		\qquad \text{whenever } \pi \in (0,1).
	\]
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:ruleinv}
	Fix an aggregate path $A \ge 0$ and an agent present on $[t_0,\tau)$.
	Under the optimal rule the agent attacks at some time if and only if
	$G(s,\tau) > 0$ for some $s \in [t_0,\tau)$, which is also the criterion
	under \eqref{eq:rule}. In particular $A \equiv 0$ is an equilibrium under
	one rule if and only if it is under the other, and the set of agents that
	ever attack against a given path is the same.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:Mref}
	$M_t \le M^{\mathrm{ref}}_t$ for every $t$ and every admissible $A \ge 0$, with
	equality for all $t$ when $\eta_{\mathrm{r}} = 0$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:rep}
	For $t<\tau$,
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:rep}
		G(t,\tau) = \pi h\,e^{-(\Phi_\tau-\Phi_t)}\big(1-e^{-k(\tau-t)}\big)
		+ \int_t^\tau e^{-[k(s-t)+\Phi_s-\Phi_t]}\big(\epsilon a \Pi_s - \eta h\big)\,ds ,
	\end{equation}
	and consequently
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:repbound}
		G(t,\tau) \;\le\; \int_t^\tau e^{-[k(s-t)+\Phi_s-\Phi_t]}\,B(s)\,ds ,
	\end{equation}
	with equality when $A \equiv 0$ on $[t,\tau]$, in which case
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:repexact}
		G(t,\tau) \;=\; \int_t^\tau e^{-k(s-t)}\,B(s)\,ds .
	\end{equation}
	In every case $G(t,\tau) = B(\tau)\,(\tau - t) + O\big((\tau-t)^2\big)$ as
	$t \uparrow \tau$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:pi}
	If $\pi = 0$ then $W_0 \equiv h$ and $X_0 \le W_0$ for all $t<\tau$
	(strictly if $\eta > 0$), so $G \le 0$ and no agent ever attacks, under
	either rule of \S\ref{sec:rule}, at any values of $\psi,\eta,a,\epsilon$ and
	any population inputs.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:pistar}
	Set
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:pistarstar}
		\pi^{\ast\ast} \;:=\; \frac{\eta}
		{\psi + \eta + \epsilon\,a\,\max_t M^{\mathrm{ref}}_t} .
	\end{equation}
	If $\pi \le \pi^{\ast\ast}$ then $G \le 0$ for all $t<\tau$ against \emph{any}
	nonnegative attacking path (strictly if $\pi < \pi^{\ast\ast}$), so
	$A \equiv 0$ is the unique equilibrium and no agent ever attacks, under
	either rule. Conversely, suppose $\pi > \pi^{\ast\ast}$ and that some agent's
	presence interval $[t_0,\tau)$ is contained in the set
	$\{s : \pi h(\psi + \epsilon a M^{\mathrm{ref}}_s) > (1-\pi)\eta h\}$, which is a
	neighborhood of $\operatorname{argmax}_t M^{\mathrm{ref}}_t$. Then that agent attacks
	against $A \equiv 0$, so $A \equiv 0$ is not an equilibrium.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:pistar}
	If $\epsilon = 0$, or if $a = 0$, the threshold is
	$\pi^\ast = \eta/(\psi+\eta)$, independent of the arrival schedule.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:tamper}
	Suppose $\psi = 0$ and $a = 0$: neither a single attacker nor the population
	collectively can alter the record of how a flag was obtained. If $\eta > 0$
	then no agent ever attacks, at any belief $\pi < 1$ and any collective weight
	$\epsilon$, against any attacking path.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:regimes}
	Let $\pi^\ast = \eta/(\psi + \eta)$ and $\pi^{**}$ be as in
	\eqref{eq:pistarstar}, so $\pi^{**} \le \pi^\ast$. In the fraction
	$N_\infty/M^{\mathrm{ev}}_\infty$ of arrivals that ever attack, the model has three
	regimes: for $\pi \le \pi^{**}$ the fraction is $0$ exactly
	(Theorem~\ref{thm:pistar}); for $\pi > \pi^\ast$ it is $1$ exactly, under
	either rule, against every equilibrium path; and for
	$\pi^{**} < \pi \le \pi^\ast$ it can be strictly between.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:reversal}
	Two explanations suggest themselves and both are wrong. It is not accumulated
	detection exposure compounding backwards through \eqref{eq:X}: with $\Pi$ held
	constant, \eqref{eq:repexact} has a constant integrand and $G$ is monotone in
	the budget at every budget and every $\tau$. Nor is it the mean field feedback:
	freezing $A \equiv 0$ while leaving $\Pi_t$ time-varying still produces the
	reversal.

	What causes it is the \emph{time-concentration of} $\Pi_t$. Since
	$\Pi_t = \pi h M_t$ and the board fills and then empties, an agent with a long
	remaining budget spends the early part of it when $\Pi$ is small and the
	collective term in $B$ is worth nothing, while the hazard accrues throughout.
	The $aA_t$ feedback roughly doubles the effect but does not create it.
	Under the optimal rule the same time-concentration produces \emph{delay}
	rather than abstention.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:ladder}
Fix $\bar n \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, rates
$0 < \psi_0 \le \psi_1 \le \dots \le \psi_{\bar n} =: \psi_{\max} < \infty$, a
discovery rate $c > 0$ and a searching weight $\theta \in [0,1]$. The public
state is a rung $n_t \in \{0, 1, \dots, \bar n\}$, $n_0 = 0$, which jumps from
$n$ to $n+1$ at rate $c S_t$ while $n < \bar n$, where
$S_t = A_t + \theta(M_t - A_t)$ is the searching mass. On rung $n$ the
private fix rate of every attacker is $\psi_n$. Nothing else changes.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:A}
$W_n(t,\tau) = W_0(t,\tau) = h - \pi h\,e^{-(\Phi_\tau - \Phi_t)}$ for every $n$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:rep-lad}
Let $k_n = \psi_n + \eta$ and
$\beta_n(s,\tau) = k_n\pi h\,e^{-(\Phi_\tau - \Phi_s)} + \epsilon a \Pi_s - \eta h$.
Then $G_n = X_n - W_0$ satisfies, for $n < \bar n$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Gn}
G_n(t,\tau) = \int_t^\tau \exp\Big(-\!\int_t^s (k_n + aA_u + cS_u)\,\mathrm{d} u\Big)
\big[\beta_n(s,\tau) + cS_s\,G_{n+1}(s,\tau)\big] \,\mathrm{d} s,
\end{equation}
and on the top rung the same with $c = 0$. In particular
$\beta_n(s,\tau) \le B_n(s) := \pi h(\psi_n + \epsilon a M_s) - (1-\pi)\eta h$:
the bracket of \eqref{eq:bracket} with the reachability of the current rung.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:guarantee}
Let $A \ge 0$ and $0 \le M_t \le \overline{M}$ be any paths. If
$\pi \le \pi^{\ast\ast}(\psi_{\max})$ then $G_n(t,\tau) \le 0$ for every rung and every
$t \le \tau$, strictly if $\pi < \pi^{\ast\ast}(\psi_{\max})$, so no agent attacks at any
rung under any stopping rule.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:onset}
Let $\theta = 0$ and $M_t = M^{\mathrm{ref}}_t$. The profile $A \equiv 0$ is an
equilibrium, starting from rung $n_0$, if and only if $\pi \le \pi^{\ast\ast}(\psi_{n_0})$.
In particular, for $\pi^{\ast\ast}(\psi_{\max}) < \pi \le \pi^{\ast\ast}(\psi_0)$ the no-attack
profile is an equilibrium and Proposition~\ref{prop:guarantee} does not
exclude an attacking one.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:pi0lad}
If $\pi = 0$ and $\eta > 0$ then $G_n(t,\tau) < 0$ for all $n$ and $t < \tau$,
for any paths $(A, M)$ and any ladder.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:lln}
For a bounded measurable path $S \ge 0$ and any $T$,
$\mathbb{E}[\sup_{t \le T} |K^\delta_t - \kappa \Sigma_t|^2] \le 4\delta\kappa\Sigma_T \to 0$
as $\delta \to 0$.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:conv}
Fix paths $(A, M)$ and a starting stock $K$. The attack value on the
$\delta$-ladder at rung $\lfloor K/\delta\rfloor$ converges, as $\delta \to 0$,
to the solution of \eqref{eq:X} with $\psi$ replaced by
$\psi_s = \psi(K + \kappa(\Sigma_s - \Sigma_t))$; likewise for $W$ and $G$.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
An unpoisoned agent with an impossible task scores $0$; with a solvable task
	it scores $h$ by hypothesis. A poisoned agent scores $h$ if $S=\mathsf L$ and
	$0$ if $S=\mathsf T$, in expectation $(1-\pi)h$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Attacking changes the population flow in exactly one way: an attacker is
	removed at rate $\eta_{\mathrm{r}}$. Arrivals are exogenous and exits occur at $t = \tau$
	with $\tau$ fixed at arrival, so neither depends on $A$. Hence $M$ is
	$M^{\mathrm{ref}}$ less the removed mass whose exit time still lies ahead, and equals it
	when $\eta_{\mathrm{r}} = 0$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Solving \eqref{eq:W} with $u := h-W_0$ gives $\partial_t u = aA_t u$,
	$u(\tau) = \pi h$, hence $W_0(t,\tau) = h - \pi h\,e^{-(\Phi_\tau-\Phi_t)}$.
	Subtracting \eqref{eq:W} from \eqref{eq:X} and writing $X_0 = G + W_0$,
	\[
		\partial_t G = (k + aA_t)G + k\,W_0 - \psi h - \epsilon a \Pi_t ,
		\qquad G(\tau,\tau) = 0 ,
	\]
	and $k W_0 - \psi h = \eta h - k\pi h\,e^{-(\Phi_\tau-\Phi_t)}$. Applying
	variation of constants, the $s$-dependence of the $W_0$ term telescopes,
	because $e^{-(\Phi_s-\Phi_t)}e^{-(\Phi_\tau-\Phi_s)}$ does not depend on $s$.
	What survives is \eqref{eq:rep}.

	For \eqref{eq:repbound}, write $1-e^{-k(\tau-t)} = \int_t^\tau k e^{-k(s-t)}ds$
	and note $\Phi$ is nondecreasing, so $e^{-(\Phi_\tau-\Phi_t)} \le
	e^{-(\Phi_s-\Phi_t)}$ for $s \le \tau$. Hence the first term of \eqref{eq:rep}
	is at most $\int_t^\tau k\pi h\,e^{-[k(s-t)+\Phi_s-\Phi_t]}ds$; adding the
	integral and using $k\pi h - \eta h = \psi\pi h - \eta(1-\pi)h$ gives
	\eqref{eq:repbound}. If $A \equiv 0$ then $\Phi_\tau = \Phi_s$ on the
	interval and the inequality is an identity. The expansion as $t \uparrow
	\tau$ follows from \eqref{eq:rep} directly: the first term is
	$\pi h k(\tau-t) + O((\tau-t)^2)$ and the integral is
	$(\epsilon a \Pi_\tau - \eta h)(\tau - t) + O((\tau-t)^2)$, and
	$k\pi h - \eta h + \epsilon a \Pi_\tau = B(\tau)$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Before an attack the only randomness is the arrival of $R$, after which
	nobody attacks; so a stopping time is a deterministic time at which to
	attack if $R$ has not yet arrived, and the value of ``attack at $s$'' from
	$(t,\tau)$ is $\int_t^s aA_r e^{-(\Phi_r - \Phi_t)}h\,dr + e^{-(\Phi_s - \Phi_t)}X_0(s,\tau)$.
	The supremum $V$ over $s \in [t,\tau]$ (with $s = \tau$ meaning never) is
	Lipschitz in $t$, satisfies the dynamic programming principle over any
	$[t, t']$, and hence $V \ge X_0$ with $-\partial_t V - aA_t(h - V) \ge 0$
	a.e., with equality wherever $V > X_0$; uniqueness follows by a comparison
	argument for the linear operator, and the first hitting time of
	$\{V = X_0\}$ is optimal. The discrete recursion of \S\ref{sec:rule} is
	the same dynamic programming principle on one cell with $aA$ constant
	there.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Fix the path and the agent. For a deterministic time $s \in [t_0,\tau)$, the
	strategy ``attack at $s$ if $R$ has not arrived'' has value
	\[
		\int_{t_0}^{s} aA_r\, e^{-(\Phi_r-\Phi_{t_0})}\,h\,dr + e^{-(\Phi_s-\Phi_{t_0})}X_0(s,\tau),
	\]
	and never attacking has the same integral with $W_0(s,\tau)$ in place of
	$X_0(s,\tau)$. Their difference is $e^{-(\Phi_s-\Phi_{t_0})}G(s,\tau)$.
	Since the only information that arrives before an attack is whether $R$ has
	arrived, and nobody attacks after it has, every stopping time is of this
	form. Hence $V(t_0,\tau) > W_0(t_0,\tau)$ --- the optimizer attacks at some
	time --- if and only if $G(s,\tau) > 0$ for some $s \in [t_0,\tau)$, which is
	also the condition for the first-passage rule ever to fire.

	For the claim in \S\ref{sec:rule} that the rules can differ: if $B < 0$ on
	$[t, s_1)$ and $A \equiv 0$, then by \eqref{eq:repexact}
	$G(t,\tau) = \int_t^{s_1} e^{-k(s-t)}B\,ds + e^{-k(s_1-t)}G(s_1,\tau) <
	e^{-k(s_1-t)}G(s_1,\tau)$, so attacking at $s_1$ strictly beats attacking at
	$t$ even when $G(t,\tau) > 0$, and the first-passage rule attacks at $t$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
At $\pi = 0$, \eqref{eq:W} has terminal value $W_0(\tau,\tau) = h$ and
	$\partial_t W_0 = -aA_t(h-W_0)$; the constant $W_0 \equiv h$ solves it, and
	the equation is linear, so this is the solution. For $X_0$, note
	$\Pi_t = \pi h M_t = 0$, so \eqref{eq:X} reads $\partial_t X_0 = (\psi +
	aA_t + \eta)X_0 - (\psi + aA_t)h$ with $X_0(\tau,\tau) = h$. At
	$X_0 = h$ the right-hand side equals $\eta h \ge 0$, so integrating backwards
	from $\tau$ gives $X_0 < h$ for $t < \tau$ whenever $\eta > 0$, and
	$X_0 \equiv h$ when $\eta = 0$. In either case $G = X_0 - W_0 \le 0$ for every
	$t < \tau$, so by Lemma~\ref{lem:ruleinv} no agent ever attacks under either
	rule.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Suppose $\pi \le \pi^{\ast\ast}$ and let $A \ge 0$ be arbitrary. By
	Lemma~\ref{lem:Mref}, $\Pi_s = \pi h M_s \le \pi h \max_t M^{\mathrm{ref}}_t$, so
	\[
		B(s) \;\le\; h\Big[\pi\big(\psi+\eta+\epsilon a \max\nolimits_t M^{\mathrm{ref}}_t\big)
		- \eta\Big] \;\le\; 0 .
	\]
	By \eqref{eq:repbound}, $G \le 0$ everywhere, so by Lemma~\ref{lem:ruleinv}
	the best response to $A$ is not to attack and the only fixed point is
	$A \equiv 0$. If $\pi < \pi^{\ast\ast}$ the displayed bound is strict, so
	$B < 0$ on all of $[t,\tau]$ and $G < 0$. (At $\pi = \pi^{\ast\ast}$ exactly,
	$G$ can vanish on budgets spent entirely where $M^{\mathrm{ref}}$ sits at its maximum; the
	conclusion is unaffected because attacking requires $G > 0$.)

	Conversely, take $A \equiv 0$, so $M = M^{\mathrm{ref}}$ and \eqref{eq:repexact}
	applies. The set $U := \{s : \pi h(\psi + \epsilon a M^{\mathrm{ref}}_s) > (1-\pi)\eta h\}$
	is exactly $\{B > 0\}$ on this path; if $\pi > \pi^{**}$ it contains
	$\operatorname{argmax}_t M^{\mathrm{ref}}_t$, and it is a neighborhood of it when
	$M^{\mathrm{ref}}$ is continuous there, or contains the interval on which the maximum is
	attained when $M^{\mathrm{ref}}$ is piecewise constant. For an agent whose presence
	interval $[t_0,\tau)$ lies in $U$, $B > 0$ on $[t_0,\tau]$ and
	\eqref{eq:repexact} gives $G(t_0,\tau) > 0$, so that agent attacks and
	$A \equiv 0$ is not an equilibrium.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
With $\psi = a = 0$ the bracket \eqref{eq:bracket} is
	$B(s) = -\eta(1-\pi)h$, a negative constant whenever $\eta > 0$ and
	$\pi < 1$. Since $a = 0$, $\Phi \equiv 0$ for \emph{every} attacking path,
	so \eqref{eq:rep} reduces to \eqref{eq:repexact} whatever $A$ is, with
	$k = \eta$, and gives
	$G(t,\tau) = -(1-\pi)h\,(1-e^{-\eta(\tau-t)}) < 0$ for every $t < \tau$.
	Attacking is never worthwhile against any attacking path, so the only
	equilibrium is $A \equiv 0$. At $\eta = 0$ the same computation gives
	$G \equiv 0$.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
The first regime is Theorem~\ref{thm:pistar}. For the second, if
	$\pi > \pi^\ast$ then $\pi(\psi + \eta) > \eta$, so
	$B(s) \ge \psi\pi h - \eta(1-\pi)h = h[\pi(\psi+\eta) - \eta] > 0$ for every
	$s$ and every path. By the last clause of Lemma~\ref{lem:rep},
	$G(t,\tau) > 0$ for $t$ sufficiently close to $\tau$, so by
	Lemma~\ref{lem:ruleinv} every agent attacks at some time under either rule.
	The third regime is the complement, and \S\ref{sec:numerics} exhibits
	interior values in it.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
For constant $A$ and $\Delta := \tau - t$, \eqref{eq:rep} reads
	$G = \pi h e^{-aA\Delta}(1 - e^{-k\Delta}) + (\epsilon a \Pi - \eta h)\,
	(1 - e^{-(k+aA)\Delta})/(k + aA)$ with $\Pi$ frozen. Expanding to second
	order in $\Delta$ and differentiating in $A$ gives
	$\partial G/\partialA = a\Delta^2\big(\tfrac12(\eta h - \epsilon a\Pi) - \pi h k\big) + O(\Delta^3)$,
	which at $\Pi = 0$ is negative exactly when $\pi(\psi+\eta) > \eta/2$.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
$W_0$ solves \eqref{eq:W} with the right terminal value; substituting
$W_n \equiv W_0$ for all $n$ into \eqref{eq:Wn} makes the jump term vanish and
reduces each equation to \eqref{eq:W}. The system is linear with bounded
coefficients on $\{t \le \tau\}$, so this is its unique bounded solution.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Subtracting \eqref{eq:W} from \eqref{eq:Xn} and using Lemma~\ref{lem:A},
\[
-\partial_t G_n = -(k_n + aA_t + cS_t)G_n + \psi_n(h - W_0) - \eta W_0
+ \epsilon a\Pi_t + cS_t G_{n+1} .
\]
Now $h - W_0 = \pi h e^{-(\Phi_\tau - \Phi_t)}$
and $-\eta W_0 = -\eta h + \eta\pi h e^{-(\Phi_\tau - \Phi_t)}$, so the source is
$\beta_n + cS_t G_{n+1}$; with $G_n(\tau,\tau) = 0$, variation of constants
gives \eqref{eq:Gn}. The bound on $\beta_n$ is $e^{-(\Phi_\tau - \Phi_s)} \le 1$.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
By the bound and $\psi_n \le \psi_{\max}$,
\[
\beta_n(s,\tau) \le h\big[\pi(\psi_{\max} + \eta + \epsilon a\overline{M}) - \eta\big] \le 0,
\]
strictly if $\pi < \pi^{\ast\ast}(\psi_{\max})$. On the top rung $G_{\bar n}$ is the
integral of a nonpositive source against a positive kernel; if $G_{n+1} \le 0$
then the source in \eqref{eq:Gn} is $\le 0$ and $G_n \le 0$. Descend. For
$\bar n = \infty$, truncate at $N$ with $\psi_n = \psi_{\max}$ for $n \ge N$ and
let $N \to \infty$. Then $X_n \le W_0 \le C_n$ and attacking is never optimal.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
At $A \equiv 0$ and $\theta = 0$, $S \equiv 0$: no discovery is made, the
rung stays at $n_0$, $\Phi \equiv 0$, and \eqref{eq:Gn} reduces to
\[
G_{n_0}(t,\tau) = \int_t^\tau e^{-k_{n_0}(s-t)}\,h\big[\pi(k_{n_0} + \epsilon a M_s) - \eta\big]\,ds .
\]
If $\pi \le \pi^{\ast\ast}(\psi_{n_0})$ the integrand is $\le 0$ for all $s$ and nobody
attacks. If $\pi > \pi^{\ast\ast}(\psi_{n_0})$ the integrand is positive on
$\{s : M_s > \overline{M} - \delta\}$ for some $\delta > 0$, a set of positive
measure, so $G_{n_0}(t,\tau) > 0$ for some $t < \tau$ bracketing a point of
it; by Lemma~\ref{lem:ruleinv} that cell attacks under the optimal rule too.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
At $\pi = 0$, $\Pi \equiv 0$ and $\beta_n \equiv -\eta h < 0$; descend as above.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
$n_t$ is a counting process with intensity $\lambda_t = \kappa S_t/\delta$, so
$m_t = n_t - \int_0^t \lambda_s\,ds$ is a square-integrable martingale with
$\mathbb{E}[m_T^2] = \mathbb{E}\int_0^T \lambda_s\,ds = \kappa\Sigma_T/\delta$~\cite{bremaud}.
Since $K^\delta_t - \kappa\Sigma_t = \delta m_t$, Doob's $L^2$ inequality~\cite{ry99} gives
$\mathbb{E}\sup_{t \le T}(\delta m_t)^2 \le 4\delta^2\mathbb{E}[m_T^2] = 4\delta\kappa\Sigma_T$.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Equation \eqref{eq:Xn} is the backward Kolmogorov equation~\cite{ek86} of the payoff
\[
h\1_{\{\sigma_F \wedge \sigma_R < \tau \wedge \sigma_\eta\}}
+ (1-\pi)h\1_{\{\tau < \sigma_F \wedge \sigma_R \wedge \sigma_\eta\}}
+ \int_t^{\tau \wedge \sigma_F \wedge \sigma_R \wedge \sigma_\eta} \epsilon a\Pi_s\,ds ,
\]
where, conditionally on the rung path, $\sigma_F$ has hazard $\psi(K^\delta_s)$,
$\sigma_R$ has hazard $aA_s$, $\sigma_\eta$ has hazard $\eta$, and the three
are conditionally independent. Integrating out the three clocks, the value is
$\mathbb{E}[F(\psi(K^\delta_\cdot))]$ for a functional $F$ of the fix-hazard path on
$[t,\tau]$ that is bounded by $h + \epsilon a\pi h\overline{M}(\tau - t)$ and continuous
in $L^1(t,\tau)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:lln} and the Lipschitz property of $\psi$,
$\psi(K^\delta_\cdot) \to \psi(K + \kappa(\Sigma_\cdot - \Sigma_t))$ in
probability in $L^1(t,\tau)$; bounded convergence gives the claim, and
$F(\psi(K_\cdot))$ is the Feynman--Kac representation~\cite{ek86} of the limit equation.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
